plan.title: Improve top-level directive help output and command discovery

narratives.Description: Improve top-level directive help output and command discovery. This story closes the linked GitHub issue with a scoped fix, tests, and a CHANGELOG entry. File scope and verify commands are recorded under plan.metadata.swarm for concurrent allocation.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The top-level `directive` / `directive --help` output is currently an undifferentiated dump of registered verbs. It should be structured like a normal CLI help surface: title/version, usage, common options, common commands, and a clear path to the full command list.

## Current behavior

Running `directive` or `directive --help` prints:

- `Usage: directive <verb> [args...]`
- a long `Registered verbs:` list
- both canonical and alias forms such as `verify-branch` and `verify:branch`
- no introductory description
- no command categories
- no explanation of common options such as `--help`, `-h`, `--version`, or `-V`
- no version in the help title, even though `--version` exists

This is difficult for humans and first-time users to scan.

## Proposed behavior

Replace the top-level help spew with a curated help page:

- Title including tool name and major/minor version, for example `Directive v0.x`.
- One-line description of what Directive does.
- Usage forms:
  - `directive <command> [options]`
  - `directive help`
  - `directive commands` or equivalent for the full list.
- Common options:
  - `-h, --help`
  - `-V, --version`
- Common verbs grouped by workflow, such as:
  - `doctor`
  - `session:start`
  - `check`
  - `triage:welcome`
  - `triage:queue`
  - `scope:promote`
  - `project:render`
  - `spec:render`
- A clear note that colon-style task verbs are preferred in help, while dash-style aliases may remain supported for compatibility.
- A separate full-list command or flag for exhaustive output.

## Acceptance criteria

- `directive` and `directive --help` print concise, categorized help rather than every registered verb.
- `directive --version` prints only version information.
- Help output documents common options.
- The exhaustive registered-verb list remains available through an explicit command or flag.
- Help avoids listing both dash and colon aliases unless explicitly showing aliases.
- Tests snapshot the top-level help output and version output.

## Related

Related but not duplicate: #1150 covers categorized help for `task triage` / `task scope`; #49 covered version display on command startup; #1669 tracks broader distributable CLI work.
narratives.UserStory: As a CLI user, I want structured top-level directive --help, so that I can discover common commands without an undifferentiated verb dump.
